title: Quadratic approximation
goal: Upgrade your tangent-line estimate by adding a $\frac{1}{2}f''(a)(x - a)^2$ bend term so your parabola hugs the curve as it curves away from the line.

beforeThis.skill: Why is there a $\frac{1}{2}$ in front of $f''(a)(x - a)^2$? Because when you take two derivatives of $(x - a)^2$, the $2$ comes down and cancels the $\frac{1}{2}$, leaving $f''(a)$!

seeIt.title: Taylor series (Ch. 11 of Essence of Calculus)
seeIt.creator: 3Blue1Brown
seeIt.watchFor: Shows why adding the quadratic term $\frac{1}{2}f''(a)(x - a)^2$ matches the bending of $f(x)$ at $x = a$.

slowWalkthrough.creator: Professor Leonard

questions.asking: Find the exact values of $f(3)$, $f'(3)$, and $f''(3)$ from the given quadratic approximation at $x = 3$, and state whether $f'''(3)$ can be determined.
questions.statement:
The quadratic approximation of a function $f(x)$ about $x = 3$ is

$$f(x) \approx -x^2 + 6x$$

What are the values of $f(3)$, $f'(3)$, $f''(3)$, and $f'''(3)$?

questions.asking: Calculate the second-degree polynomial approximation of $\log x$ centered at $a = 1$ and evaluate it at $x = 0.93$.
questions.statement:
Use a quadratic approximation to estimate $\log(0.93)$.

(Remember we use $\log x$ to mean the natural logarithm of $x$, $\log_e x$.)

questions.asking: Plug $x = 1$ into the degree-$2$ Maclaurin polynomial for $e^x$ ($T_2(x) = 1 + x + \frac{1}{2}x^2$) to estimate $e^1$.
questions.statement: Use a quadratic approximation of $e^x$ to estimate $e$ as a decimal.
